title: When the Contact Breaks
premise: Oscar Sandoval, a former air-crash investigator living under a borrowed name, lost her husband and daughter in the crash of Flight 4471 — a crash she was forced to help cover up. When a burner phone rings with her dead husband's voice on the line, she is pulled back into the world of Vantage, the intelligence contractor that faked his death and now wants her to extract a defector who carries proof of what really happened to row twelve. As Oscar runs the extraction across three countries, she discovers the defector is bait in a trap designed to flush out everyone who knows the truth — including her. In the end, Oscar chooses love over duty, burning her own legend to expose the crash's true cause and reclaiming her name, though not without losing the last person who remembered who she used to be.
about_author: Lior Ishikawa is the pen name of a former aviation safety analyst who spent a decade reviewing black-box transcripts before turning to fiction. They write from a coastal town where fog rolls in most mornings, and they have never once flown in row twelve.

chapters.title: Row Twelve
chapters.summary: POV: Oscar. On the fifth anniversary of Flight 4471, Oscar attends the memorial under her assumed name, laying flowers for a family no one knows was hers. A flashback reveals she signed the final report knowing the data was altered. The emotional beat is grief worn as camouflage — until she finds a burner phone taped beneath her car's seat, ringing.

chapters.title: The Voice That Shouldn't Call
chapters.summary: POV: Oscar. The phone rings again; the voice is unmistakably her husband Daniel's, reciting a phrase only he knew. He tells her a defector named Ilse Brandt has evidence about the crash and names a rendezvous in Rotterdam. Oscar checks the phone's provenance and finds it manufactured by Vantage. The beat: terror braided with hope she doesn't trust.

chapters.title: The Go-Bag Rule
chapters.summary: POV: Oscar, with an interlude from Vantage handler Marcus Reeve. Oscar decides to run the job herself rather than report it, packing the go-bag she's kept ready for five years. Reeve, meanwhile, reports to superiors that 'the widow' has taken the hook. The beat: cold competence masking a decision made with her heart, not her tradecraft.

chapters.title: Rotterdam Static
chapters.summary: POV: Oscar. In Rotterdam, Oscar makes contact with Ilse Brandt, a sharp, frightened analyst carrying an encrypted drive. Ilse recognizes Oscar's real name from the crash file and accuses her of complicity. Their uneasy alliance forms over a single condition: Ilse will only talk once they're out of the country. The beat: guilt meeting its witness.

chapters.title: Dead Drop Weather
chapters.summary: POV: alternating Oscar and Reeve. The extraction plan hits interference — a second team is shadowing them, one Reeve claims he didn't field. Oscar realizes someone inside Vantage wants both women dead before the drive surfaces. A near-miss at the train station costs them their safe route. The beat: paranoia sharpening into clarity.

chapters.title: What the Black Box Kept
chapters.summary: POV: Ilse. Through Ilse's eyes, we learn the drive contains raw flight-data showing a software fault Vantage sold to the airline — and that Daniel Sandoval discovered it days before the flight. Ilse reveals Daniel wasn't on the passenger manifest; he was aboard deliberately, investigating. The beat: the ground tilts under everything Oscar believed.

chapters.title: The Bait Confesses
chapters.summary: POV: Oscar. Cornered in a safehouse, Oscar decrypts part of the drive and finds a message Daniel recorded before boarding: if you're hearing this, I'm already gone — trust the voice, not the caller. She understands the phone calls are synthesized, a lure built from his voiceprints. The beat: heartbreak weaponized; she keeps moving anyway.

chapters.title: Three Minutes Over the North Sea
chapters.summary: POV: Oscar and Reeve converging. Reeve corners them at a coastal airstrip, revealing the trap: Vantage needed Oscar to lead them to the drive's backup, held by a journalist in Copenhagen. But Reeve hesitates — his own brother died in row twelve, and he's read the file. The beat: duty cracking along a personal fault line.

chapters.title: Everything Burns Cleaner Than Lies
chapters.summary: POV: Oscar. Climax. With Reeve's reluctant help, Oscar broadcasts the flight data and Daniel's recording to regulators and press simultaneously, then faces down the Vantage strike team long enough for Ilse and the journalist to escape. Reeve takes a bullet covering her retreat. The beat: love against duty resolved — she saves the truth, not herself.

chapters.title: Oscar Sandoval, Investigator
chapters.summary: POV: Oscar, epilogue six months later. The crash is reopened; Vantage executives are indicted. Oscar testifies under her real name for the first time in five years, then visits two graves — her daughter's, and Reeve's. The burner phone sits in an evidence bag, silent at last. The beat: identity reclaimed, memory honored, grief finally allowed to be just grief.
